products.title: Assessment With Gender-Diverse Clients and Current Trends
products.body_html:
Friday, February 5, 2027, 1:00 to 4:00 PM Eastern. Live on Zoom. Ten seats.

A three-hour live workshop for clinicians who evaluate gender-diverse clients, and for clinicians who refer for evaluation and read the reports.

Assessment is often treated as neutral. It is not. Intake language, norm selection, instrument design, and interpretive habits can all reduce validity when a client is transgender or gender diverse, and the errors rarely announce themselves in the score report. This workshop works through where bias enters the assessment workflow and what a defensible evaluation does about it.

What we cover

The workflow before any instrument is given. Intake language, consent, and the documentation choices that shape everything after them.

Where norms and instruments do not fit. How standard norming and instrument design can fail a gender-diverse client, and how to state that limitation in the interpretation rather than hide it.

The differential. Distinguishing gender-related distress from co-occurring presentations that are commonly conflated with it, worked through a case.

Report language. Writing findings that are accurate, affirming, and usable by the reader, including what the evaluation cannot conclude.

The current environment. What the present legal, policy, and referral landscape changes in referral questions, norming, and documentation.

Who this is for

Licensed psychologists and licensed mental health clinicians who conduct psychological evaluations, and clinicians who refer for evaluation and want to read reports with sharper questions.

Format and tuition

Three hours, live on Zoom, capped at ten. Tuition $99. The Zoom link and materials go by email to registrants before the session.

Continuing education

This workshop does not award continuing education credit.

Led by Niki Serravalle, Psy.D., LPCMH, NCC, a licensed psychologist whose practice centers on psychological evaluation.

products.title: Nature-Informed EMDR: Ethical and Clinically Grounded Applications for Preparation, Regulation, and Integration
products.body_html:
EMDRIA Approved for 3 EMDRIA Credits.

This three-hour workshop is for EMDR clinicians who already know how to do the work and want to think more carefully about when and how nature-informed elements belong inside a standard EMDR case. It is not a new protocol. The eight-phase, three-pronged structure does not change.

The course examines how environmental context, sensory grounding, and ecologically attuned elements can act as adjunctive supports during preparation, affect regulation, and integration. Three modalities are addressed: brought-in natural objects, virtual or representational nature contact, and in-person outdoor or window-mediated work. Contraindications, accessibility, and decision-making sit alongside the technique-level content rather than at the end as an afterthought.

Date and time. Friday, March 5, 2027. 1:00 PM to 4:00 PM Eastern.

Format. Live webinar via Zoom. Real-time, interactive, with chat and verbal participation. EMDRIA Credit is granted only to participants who attend live, in real time. Ten seats.

Tuition. $99.

Continuing education. This program has been approved for 3 EMDRIA Credits.

Prerequisite. Completion of an EMDRIA-Approved Basic EMDR Training. Eligibility for EMDRIA Credits is restricted to clinicians who have completed an EMDRIA-Approved Basic EMDR Training.

Learning objectives. By the end of this 3-hour workshop, participants will be able to:

  1. Describe at least three ways environmental context may influence affect regulation, grounding, and treatment readiness in EMDR.
  2. Differentiate standard EMDR procedures from adjunctive nature-informed elements used during preparation, regulation, and integration.
  3. Identify at least four clinical factors relevant to nature-informed EMDR work, including dissociation risk, accessibility, privacy, and environmental unpredictability.
  4. Apply at least three nature-informed strategies to EMDR preparation or integration using clinical examples.
  5. Evaluate when a nature-informed element is clinically indicated, contraindicated, or outside the scope of standard EMDR procedure.

What you receive. Live three-hour workshop attendance. Participant workbook with embedded quick-reference, decision tree, six clinical activities, and a 30-day action plan. Reference list and EMDRIA Definition of EMDR handout. Certificate of completion upon attendance verification and evaluation submission.

Presenter. Niki Serravalle, PsyD, LPCMH, NCC, is a licensed clinical psychologist, EMDRIA Certified Therapist, and EMDRIA Approved Consultant. She is the founder of Center for Balanced Living and CFBL Institute. Her clinical focus is complex trauma, integrative case conceptualization, and psychological assessment.

Required statements. This program has been approved for 3 EMDRIA Credits. CFBL Institute maintains responsibility for this program and its content in accordance with EMDRIA requirements. Full EMDR Training Required. Eligibility for EMDRIA Credits is restricted to clinicians who have completed an EMDRIA-Approved Basic EMDR Training. The program site is ADA compliant. Please contact Dr. Niki Serravalle at drserravalle@gmail.com if you require accommodations. There is no commercial support for this program.

products.title: Parenting With Purpose: Monthly Parent Workshop
products.body_html:
Parenting With Purpose: Monthly Parent Workshop

Led by Brianna Patton, LACMH, NCC. Meets once a month, online. The next session is Friday, December 4. The time and Zoom link go by email to everyone who registers.

Parenting does not come with a manual, and every stage brings new questions. Whether you’re navigating emotional outbursts, growing independence, school stress, anxiety, or the everyday challenges of raising children and teens, you don’t have to figure it out alone.

Parenting With Purpose is a monthly virtual workshop for parents and caregivers who want practical strategies, professional guidance, and a supportive community of other parents.

Each session focuses on a different parenting topic while providing opportunities for discussion, reflection, and skill-building that you can immediately apply at home.

Registration is free. Questions? Email Brianna at bpatton@balancedlivingde.com.

products.title: Foundations of Trauma Therapy: 12-Week Integration Course
products.body_html:
Founding cohort. Wednesdays, 5:00 to 6:00 PM Eastern, January 13 through April 7, 2027, with no session February 17. Twelve live sessions, virtual. Ten seats.

Every clinician trained in a model eventually meets the client for whom it stops working. Breath work, and the client cannot stop perseverating on thoughts. Reprocessing, and body sensation overwhelms what containment can hold. This course is built around that moment: what you see that tells you the approach has failed, what you do first, how you choose the next move and from which model, and how you know the client is ready to return to the original work.

The course moves through trauma treatment by model family. Each week reviews a family and its core skills, then turns to applying it with the models that came before. Integration accumulates across the twelve weeks.

Format

One live virtual meeting each week, 60 minutes. Enrollment is capped at ten so the time can be spent on cases and clinical skill rather than lecture.

Continuing education

The founding cohort does not award continuing education credit.

Tuition

Founding cohort rate: $395. Standard tuition for later cohorts: $595.

Who this is for

Licensed psychologists, licensed professional counselors, clinical social workers, and associates under supervision.

Led by Niki Serravalle, Psy.D., LPCMH, NCC.

products.title: Differential Diagnosis: ADHD, Anxiety, and Trauma
products.body_html:
Friday, January 22, 2027, 1:00 to 4:00 PM Eastern. Live on Zoom. Ten seats.

A three-hour live virtual intensive for licensed clinicians who evaluate ADHD, or who are asked about it often enough that they need to reason about it well.

ADHD referrals have risen sharply, and a substantial portion of what arrives for evaluation is not ADHD. Sleep disruption, trauma-related attentional dysregulation, anxiety, mood disorders, specific learning disorder, and autism all generate attention complaints that elevate the same rating scales. The diagnostic question is rarely whether attentional difficulty exists. It is what is producing it, whether the onset and cross-setting criteria are genuinely met, and whether the evidence supports the conclusion you are about to put in writing and sign.

This intensive works through the reasoning rather than the checklist.

What we cover

Criteria applied with real threshold language. DSM-5-TR criteria in practice, including the childhood onset requirement and the cross-setting impairment standard that retrospective adult evaluations routinely fail to establish.

The differential as clinical work, not a list. Distinguishing ADHD from anxiety, trauma-related attentional disruption, mood disorders, sleep disorders, specific learning disorder, and autism, including the common presentations where more than one condition is genuinely present and the diagnosis is additive rather than exclusive.

What rating scales can and cannot support. Informant discrepancy, base rate problems, and the particular limits of self-report in adult evaluation.

Continuous performance tests. What the literature actually supports regarding sensitivity and specificity, and why a normal CPT does not rule ADHD out and an abnormal one does not rule it in.

Validity considerations. Symptom and performance validity in adult ADHD evaluation, including how to conduct and document evaluations undertaken for stimulant access or academic accommodation.

Integration and report writing. Bringing developmental history, collateral report, records, and test data into findings that hold together, with rule-out reasoning made explicit and accommodation recommendations that survive review by a school, a university disability office, or another clinician.

Who this is for

Licensed psychologists, licensed mental health clinicians, and school psychologists who conduct or contribute to ADHD evaluations. Also appropriate for therapists who do not test but are regularly asked about ADHD and want to refer with sharper questions.

Format and tuition

Three hours, live on Zoom, capped at ten so the time goes to reasoning through cases. Tuition $99. The Zoom link and materials go by email to registrants before the session.

Continuing education

This workshop does not award continuing education credit.

Led by Niki Serravalle, Psy.D., LPCMH, NCC, a licensed psychologist whose practice centers on psychological and psychoeducational evaluation.

products.title: Foundations of Trauma Therapy: Live Virtual Intensive
products.body_html:
The next offering is the 12-week Integration Course, founding cohort beginning January 13, 2027. Reserve your seat here.

A live virtual intensive for licensed mental health clinicians who want to think across trauma modalities rather than within one. Most trauma training teaches a single model and leaves the clinician to work out when it applies. This intensive works the other direction, starting from the clinical presentation and reasoning toward the intervention.

The pilot cohort ran in September 2026. What that cohort told us shaped the 12-week course.

What the intensive covers

Case conceptualization across modalities, matching intervention to presentation and to phase of treatment, recognizing when stabilization has to precede processing, and working with clients whose trauma history does not present as trauma.

Who this is for

Licensed psychologists, licensed professional counselors, clinical social workers, and associates under supervision.

Led by Niki Serravalle, Psy.D., LPCMH, NCC.
